text:
alex: heads up — saw a ~12% token-latency regression on one of the dedicated pools after yesterday's kernel routing tweak. stack: serving-runtime v2.4.1 -> v2.4.2
perf-bot: alert: latency_p50 increased 12% on pool-gpu-a (alert id 2258675309) :rotating_light:
maria: can you paste the microbench you used? is it seq-len dependent?
alex: repro is seq_len=64 and 128. 64 is fine, 128 shows the regression. i ran the microbench on a single node: quick log below
```
$ ./runtime_bench --model llama-7b --seq 128 --batch 1 --repeat 50
p50  : 43.2ms (v2.4.1) -> 48.4ms (v2.4.2)
mean : 45.0ms -> 50.1ms
kernel route switched from sm_fastpath_kv to sm_generic_kv on this node
```
kevin: hmm. that node is an sm_86 GPU but the probe reported "tensor_cores: available" and we routed to fp8/bf16-optimized kernels which are slower at seqlen=128 on this driver combo. i suspect capprobe false-positive on tc support after the driver update.
dina: also noticed increased kv-cache misses during the run — we saw more cache invalidations when the slower kernel hit, causing more prefix rebuilds. could amplify latency.
maria: can we confirm the probe output? alex, paste output of gpu-capprobe --dump for that node
alex: pasted: 
```
GPU: sm86
driver: 538.12
caps: TF32:true BF16:true FP8:true
heuristics_version: 3
selected_kernel_hint: tensorcore_kv_fastpath
```
kevin: driver 538.12 has a known quirk with BF16 math partitioning — we should validate by running a tiny tensorcore micro-op instead of trusting reported caps. proposal: add a lightweight runtime sampler that executes a 1-2 batch micro-op during boot to verify tensorcore BF16/FP8 latency behavior across seq lengths. fallback to non-tc kernels if sample shows higher latency.
maria: i like that. keep probe cheap and opt-in via a node label so we don't add startup jitter everywhere. maybe run sampling in background and mark node as "validated" once done.
dina: +1. also record kv-cache hit rate during sample so we can correlate. if sample itself triggers thrash we need to abort.
kevin: sketch of sampler command:
```
// run from runtime agent
/redwood/bin/gpu_probe_sample --seq-lens 64,128 --reps 10 --ops micro-gemm-bf16 --max-ms 200
// outputs CSV: seq_len,kernel,median_ms,kv_miss_rate
```
alex: if we do that we should also add a sequencelen-gating rule: for seq_len > 96 prefer generic_kv unless sampler shows tc_win_ms < generic_ms - 5%. avoids up-switching for long prefixes.
maria: we should add a small unit test harness that fuzzes driver-reported caps vs sampled perf and ensures the router picks the right kernel. also add a perf regression alert for the sampling metric so we don't silently flip.
perf-bot: noted: create perf-check ticket if sample->route flip occurs more than 3 times in 24h (rule 7).
dina: created draft PR branch sm-sampler-guard. putting a WIP in github: github.com/redwood/runtime/pulls/4872
kevin: can one of you run the sampler on the affected node and paste CSV results?
alex: running now, will post soon.
(10 minutes later)
alex: results pasted:
```
seq_len,kernel,median_ms,kv_miss_rate
64,tensorcore_kv,21.3,0.02
128,tensorcore_kv,49.1,0.18
64,generic_kv,24.5,0.02
128,generic_kv,45.0,0.09
```
kevin: those numbers confirm it — tensorcore_kv is faster at 64 but much worse at 128, and kv miss rate jumps with the tensorcore path. sampler should mark this node as "prefer_generic_for_long_seqs".
maria: action items: (1) kevin to land sampler POC + gating logic (PR 4872), (2) dina to add kv hit-rate capture to sampler metrics, (3) alex to roll node label and run fleet sampling, (4) add alert for route flips.
alex: i'll run fleet sampling during the next maintenance window.
kevin: i'll add config toggles: sample_enabled, sample_timeout_ms=500, seqlen_threshold=96. also will write e2e test.
dina: thanks — this should reduce these weird regressions. :100:
alex: good catch everyone. closing thread after PRs land.
